newsitem.title: DENMARK: BG Bank sees lower 1997 core earnings.
newsitem.headline: BG Bank sees lower 1997 core earnings.

text.p: Denmark's third biggest bank BG Bank said on Monday it expected slightly lower core earnings in 1997 than 1996.

"Core earnings in 1997 are expected to be at a slightly lower level than in 1996 as net interest and fee income - due to the narrowing of interest margins and ongoing low interest rates - are not expected to be fully offset by lower operating costs or debt or depreciation provisions," BG Bank said in a statement accompanying its result.
BG Bank's core earnings rose in 1996 to 1.665 billion crowns from 1995's 1.113 billion crowns.
"Provided that the Danish economy continues to develop in a stable fashion, losses and provisions are expected to show a modest fall in 1997," it said.
BG Bank said that operating costs in 1997 would still have to match activity levels, meaning that staff cuts would be necessary during the present year.

"In 1997 we foresee stable growth and a moderate rise in demand for financial services. Competition in both private and business customer areas is expected to intensify further, bringing net interest income under pressure," it said.
